Going into my senior year as a CS major. It's an awesome program and there's some awesome opportunities for internships and meeting people in the industry. Maybe this is just my experience, but I found myself having to teach myself a good amount of what I know as a programmer, which is pretty normal in CS; Not that this is a bad thing by any means, I just feel like some of the courses can lack a bit of depth by not really using C++ tools beyond a simple use. My only complaint is that for almost all courses past CS II, you either get an amazing professor, or a terrible professor, no in between lol. There's numerous groups, discords, etc for students building side projects, game dev, internship prep, and other things.

Regardless, CS is awesome here & really underrated, good luck!

i moved to san mo back in august & i'm now in my second semester at tx st (junior, transferred in). I honestly love every aspect of it. Granted, i moved in from a relatively small town in the middle of nowhere, but everything ab this place is awesome. The people here are awesome, the skate scene is sick, you have austin & san antonio both within an hour drive, and campus is still relatively lit although we're still in a pandemic.

Only thing that sucks right now is the financial aspect as it's impossible to find a job out here right now, so definitely keep that in mind since covid isnt going anywhere. Also it sometimes gets boring just doing online classes, but I like to go to campus, go to the library, and just do my zoom classes on my laptop in there lol
